summary: Bal Krishen Thapar was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied at the University of the Punjab (~1941-1943). He served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1978-1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist. He held positions at Panjab University, where he was attested as an Assistant in 1932 and as in-charge of the Sanskrit Section in 1941.

Bangwei Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University (~1983-1987), where he later served as Professor (~1987) and Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies (~1992).
Banikanta Kakati was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1915-1918) and served as a professor at Cotton University (~1918-1949).

Barbara E. Ward studied at Newnham College (~1937-1940) and worked in Sinology. She held posts at the University of London (~1955-1973), the University of Cambridge (~1973-1983), and Newnham College (~1973-1983).

Barbara Gerke, a Tibetology scholar, earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies, Humboldt University (2011-2015), and Oxford (attested 2017).
Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Queen's University (~1958-1962) and at SOAS University of London (1969-1974).

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist educated at Barnard College, Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD) under W. Norman Brown. She served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Studies at Barnard College (~1968-1993).

Barbra R. Clayton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under G. Raj, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1893-1906) and subsequently held an academic post there from 1907 to 1944.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Leiden University, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1990-1992), and the University of Hamburg as Professor Dr. (~1992-2007).

Barend ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at Leiden University (1990), he held posts at KNAW (attested 1994), Heidelberg University, and Leiden University (attested 2002-2013).

Barry Kerzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Granada Hills Charter High School, the Keck School of Medicine of USC (~1972-1976), and UC Berkeley, and trained under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen.

Barry Sautman works in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University, New York University School of Law, and UCLA School of Law, and held a post at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1993).
Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and has served as an Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014-2019).
Basil Gould was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Winchester College (~1896-1902) and New College (~1902-1906), and later served in the Indian Civil Service (~1907-1947).

Linguist Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve studied at Princeton (~1847-1849), the University of Bonn (~1851-1852), and under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl (~1851-1853). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University (~1876-1915).

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. at Stanford, she was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley (~1987-1989) and Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989).

Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College (~1894-1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, and later attended Columbia University (~1898-1901).

Ben Jiao specializes in Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein in 2001 and served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
